leads.name: Treurbeuk, Oude Begraafplaats (Algemene Begraafplaats)
leads.why_lead: Named and dated (circa 1900) by the gemeente/HCL brochure 'Wandelroute Monumentaal Groen' (2022, top-10 entry IV) as standing between sections 2 and 3 of the old cemetery off Spanjaardslaan, with a photo. No matching entry found in the LRMB register within 20km of the city centre, and only a verbal location ('tussen tweede en derde afdeling'), not a coordinate. That path description is close to or the same as lee_004's plane tree location, so a future pass should walk the path and pin both trees individually rather than guess a coordinate from the brochure text alone. One source only; needs a second independent source or a precise coordinate before it can ship.

leads.name: Gewone plataan Oude Stadsbegraafplaats (second entry)
leads.why_lead: LRMB register nr 1692402, planted band 1850-1860, 'pad tussen afdeling 2 en 4', about 30m from the already-published lee_004 (LRMB nr 1692403, 'pad tussen afdeling 2 en 3', age 1840-1850) in the same cemetery. Register-only, one source; no second independent source found in this pass naming a second plane specifically. Owner=gemeente, visitable=ja, visible=nee.

leads.name: Pluimiep Vosseparkje (x2)
leads.species: Feather Elm (Ulmus glabra 'Exoniensis' or similar cultivar)
leads.why_lead: LRMB register nrs 1692406 and 1692405, planted band 1900-1910, same cultivar type as the already-published lee_008 (Molenstraat feather elms) but different specimens in Vosseparkje. Register-only. This pass (2026-09-09) fetched and OCR'd both the HCL 'Voetstappen in de Vosseparkwijk' walking-tour PDF and the HCL 'Wandelroute MONUMENTAAL GROEN' brochure (its Westerpark stop, entry 16) and neither mentions a pluimiep/iep by name in this park; also searched WebSearch directly for the term with no hit beyond the register itself. Second source found: none this pass. Owner=gemeente, visitable=ja, visible=ja.

leads.name: Canadese populier Vosseparkje
leads.why_lead: LRMB register nr 1692404, planted band 1890-1900, west side of Vosseparkje. Register-only. This pass (2026-09-09) checked the same two HCL PDFs (walking-tour and MONUMENTAAL GROEN brochure) and WebSearch directly; no independent mention of a Canadese populier specifically in Vosseparkje/Westerpark found (the brochure's Prinsentuin stop describes a DIFFERENT Canadian poplar, the already-published lee_007 Marilandica poplar). Second source found: none this pass. Owner=gemeente, visitable=ja, visible=onbekend.

leads.name: Kaukasische/Perzische eik, zuidoostelijke ingang Vosseparkje
leads.species: Oak, species uncertain (Quercus sp., possibly Q. macranthera or Q. castaneifolia)
leads.why_lead: LRMB register nr 1686956, planted band 1870-1880, at the south-east entrance of Vosse/Westerpark. Register-only; species itself is ambiguous in the register name. This pass (2026-09-09) checked the same two HCL PDFs and WebSearch directly; no independent mention found. Second source found: none this pass. Owner=gemeente, visitable=ja, visible=ja.

leads.name: Unnamed large tree beside the Vosseparkje wingnut ('Goudes...', possibly a golden ash or similar golden-leaved cultivar)
leads.species: Unidentified, name cut off in source (Latin/common name starting 'Goudes...')
leads.coordinate: approximately 53.2024, 5.7814 (where a park path meets Molenstraat, beside the former MTS school building)
leads.why_lead: Found 2026-09-09 while verifying the Vosseparkje Caucasian Wingnut (now lee_016): the HCL 'Voetstappen in de Vosseparkwijk' walking-tour PDF says the park path comes out onto Molenstraat 'direct na twee enorme bomen, de Kaukasische Vleugelnoot ... en een Goudes[?]' (right after two huge trees, the wingnut and a 'Goudes...'). No LRMB register entry matches this second tree, no coordinate beyond the path/Molenstraat junction, and the species name is truncated in the extracted PDF text (this environment has no pdftotext/PyPDF and text was pulled from raw PDF content streams by regex, which garbles some words). Needs a clean read of the source PDF (or a site visit) to identify the species before it can be verified.

leads.name: Gewone beuk achter De Koperen Tuin, Prinsentuin
leads.why_lead: HCL brochure top-10 entry II, dated 1874, described as having a low branch that limits the height of delivery traffic behind the De Koperen Tuin pavilion in Prinsentuin. Could not be confidently matched to any LRMB register coordinate in Prinsentuin (all register beeches there, nrs 1688389 and 1688418/1688918-equivalent already match the published lee_003 and lee_005); may be a further, distinct beech or may be one of those under a different description. Needs a site visit or a clearer source before publishing to avoid duplicating an already-live tree under a new id.

resolved_2026-09-09.name: Rode paardenkastanjes / Gewone plataan / Witte paardenkastanje, tuin Diakonessenziekenhuis
resolved_2026-09-09.outcome: Shipped as lee_019, lee_020, lee_021. Researched what now occupies the former hospital garden: the Diakonessenhuis closed in 1987 and was converted into apartments in 1988-1990; the garden survives as a landscaped courtyard now named Diaconessenpark. Checked access via OpenStreetMap (Overpass): the courtyard is tagged leisure=park, wheelchair-accessible paved footways run past all three trees, there is a public bench beside them, and no gate or access=private tag exists anywhere in the courtyard (only two low 0.6m garden walls). Judged genuinely open despite two of three register entries listing owner=particulier, and flagged accordingly. See data/research/leeuwarden-verified.json for full verify_notes.

resolved_2026-09-09.name: Libanonceder, Wijbrand de Geeststraat 42 (voor het Gabbema Gasthuis)
resolved_2026-09-09.outcome: Shipped as lee_023 with an approximate coordinate (two geocodes of the address and the institution's name agreed within about 40m). Access is genuinely uncertain: the Gabbema Gasthuis is a historic almshouse of the same kind as the already-blocked Sint Anthony Gasthuis, but OSM tags a pedestrian gate right at this point as access=permissive, foot=yes, and the brochure's own wording ('voor het Gasthuis', in front of the almshouse) reads as street-facing. Shipped flagged with an honest access caveat rather than blocked outright; a future pass should settle this on the ground or check whether the Gasthuis's own website says anything about its grounds.
